title: Varna 10. The Account of the Manifestation of the Deity Sri Gaura-Gopala in the Village of Sri Yashoda
html:
Invocation of Jagadisha; in the morning Mahaprabhu and Nityananda prepare to leave; Duhkhini faints at the separation, and the Lord tells her to install His image, promising always to dwell in it and to call her mother; the Lords go to Advaita at Shantipura; by the Lord's order a craftsman comes to Yashoda and in a single night manifests the Deity — the Lord as an infant, as He used to crawl in Duhkhini's house in Nadia — and departs; in the morning Duhkhini finds Nimai crying at the door and nurses Him; Jagadisha seats the Deity on the throne in Jagannatha's temple; the Lord appears to Jagadisha in the form of Krishna and to Duhkhini as a child; at Shantipura the Lord learns of the manifestation of His image and with Nityananda comes again to Yashoda; the Deity Sri Gaura-Gopala hides; Duhkhini cooks a meal, and the Lord asks for a third portion; the Lord's teaching on the oneness of Himself, His devotee and His Deity; the joint meal of Gaura, Nityananda and the Deity; Nityananda sees Gaura-Gopala at Duhkhini's breast and glorifies her; the Lord lets Duhkhini choose which of His forms will remain in her house, and she takes Gopala; the Lords depart; glorification of Jagadisha and Duhkhini; the author's self-abasement and signature

The tenth varna

1Glory, glory to Jagadisha, glory to the merciful one!
Be kind and show mercy to me, a sinner.

2Thus the Pandita, having passed the night awake,
came in the morning and bowed to the Lord's feet.

3Then Mahaprabhu and Prabhu Nityananda,
Both joyful, performed Their morning duties.

4Then the two Lords wished to depart,
[and the Lord] speaks sweet words to Duhkhini Devi.

5Mahaprabhu says: "Mother, I make a request to you:
now I shall go to Nilachala."1

6When Gauranga spoke these words,
Duhkhini Devi, hearing [them], fainted.

7After some time the devi regained consciousness
and, weeping, began to speak before the Lord:

8"Be pleased and show me this mercy:
let me die before Your eyes.

9How shall I live, Prabhu, not seeing You?
Hearing of Your going, my heart breaks.

10What can I say, Prabhu? You act as You will:
whatever You wish will surely come to be.

11But mercifully give me instruction:
how shall I keep my life in separation from You?"

12Having said this, the devi began to weep.
Mahaprabhu mercifully said to her:

13"Listen, mother Duhkhini, to My words:
install My image.

14In that image I shall always dwell,
and I shall call you mother.

15In whatever way you desire, whenever you desire, —
then I shall fulfil that desire."

16Having thus consoled Duhkhini
and embraced Jagadisha, the Two set out.

17Then the two Lords came to Shantipura
and, having come, stayed happily in Advaita's house.2

18[Meanwhile] at Yashoda Jagadisha in supreme joy
manifests the image of Sri Mahaprabhu.3

19How that image was installed —
of that I shall tell a little.

20There was the Lord's command to manifest the Deity,
and the Pandita was constantly anxious about it.

21By the arrangement of providence, in the evening someone came
and, bowing to the Pandita, addressed [him]:

22"Listen, sir: by caste I am a craftsman.
I have come here by Mahaprabhu's command.4

23Gauranga Sri Hari commanded me:
'Go quickly to the village of Yashoda.

24There lives a certain brahmana pandita,
named Jagadisha, famed in the world.

25His wife, the chaste Duhkhini Thakurani —
she will worship My image.

26Therefore go quickly to Jagadisha
and manifest My image.'

27Mahaprabhu gave me this command;
to carry out the Lord's command I have come here."

28When the craftsman had told all this,
Jagadisha began to dance in prema.

29Jagadisha was greatly delighted;
hearing [it], Duhkhini rejoiced in her mind.

30With devotion and care they lodged the craftsman,
and that very night the craftsman manifested the sri-murti.

31As the Lord was in childhood, when [He lived] in the town of Nadia
and crawled on His knees playing in Duhkhini's house,5 —

32manifesting [by his art] an image in that form,
the craftsman left [it] at the door and went to his own place.

33In the morning Duhkhini Devi opened the door
and saw Nimai crying at the door.

34Hastily Duhkhini took that Deity onto her lap
and, giving Him the breast, comforted [Him].

35Immersed in the ocean of prema for Gaura, Duhkhini
does not herself know where she is or what she is doing.

36Jagadisha came and saw that sri-murti;
seeing [it], in prema he prostrated himself with eight limbs.

37Seeing that Duhkhini was overwhelmed with prema,
he himself tells her what had happened before:

38"Mahaprabhu commanded that the Deity be manifested;
know for certain that this is that [His] image."

39Having said this, Jagadisha tries to bring her round,
yet the devi does not return to external awareness.

40Then Jagadisha, taking that Deity in his arms,
went joyfully to Jagannatha's temple.

41There he seated the Lord on a jewelled throne
and with his own hands rendered Him fitting service.

42In this way Jagadisha serves,
while Duhkhini, in parental love, sees [Him] in the form of a child.

43When Jagadisha performs service,
Mahaprabhu then assumes the form of Krishna.

44And when Duhkhini is alone in the house,
then the Lord plays in the form of a child.

45The Lord is a wish-fulfilling tree; knowing the feelings of His devotees,
He Himself fulfils the desires of both.

46Who else can understand the mercy of Gauranga?
Thus He performs His lilas in Jagadisha's house.

47Here, at Shantipura, in Advaita's house,
[the Lord] always passes the time joyfully with the devotees.

48Learning that [His] image had become manifest in Yashoda,
the Lord felt delight in His mind.

49Mahaprabhu says: "Listen, Nityananda Raya:
My Deity has become manifest in Yashoda."

50Nityananda says: "Prabhu, You are an ocean of mercy;
to fulfil the desires of devotees is Your nature.

51Jagadisha Pandita is Your dear devotee;
You have made his glory manifest to the world.

52Jagadisha Pandita is supremely fortunate:
You, Bhagavan, have come under the sway of his prema.

53How vast is Jagadisha Pandita's good fortune:
sitting at home, he constantly sees Your feet!"

54Then the Lord humbly said to Him:
"Be kind, let us go to Jagadisha's abode.

55What My image that has appeared there is like —
going there, I shall certainly see it."

56Receiving the command, that very moment Nityananda Raya
went there together with Mahaprabhu.

57The two Lords set out in supreme delight
and, arriving, happily entered Jagadisha's house.

58Pandita Thakura, seeing the two Lords,
fell at [Their] feet, prostrate like a rod.

59Joining his palms, he offered many praises;
the two Lords embraced the Pandita.

60Then Jagadisha, bringing fragrant water,
washed the lotus feet of Both.

61There the Pandita saw Gaura Bhagavan:
sitting on Duhkhini's lap, He sucks at the breast.

62[The Pandita] announced there the arrival of the two Lords,
and Sri Gaura-Gopala began to speak to her:

63"Hide Me inside the house
and with joy in your heart serve the two Lords."

64Having said this to her, Sri Gaura-Gopala,
the Lord, at that moment assumed the form of the Deity.

65Having secretly hidden Gopala, Duhkhini
herself came to the two Lords.

66Coming, the devi bowed down, prostrate like a rod,
and, standing, with tears in her eyes gazes at [Their] form.

67The Lord asked her whether all was well.
Joining her palms, Duhkhini Devi replies:

68"By the grace of Your feet all is well;
no sorrow weighs upon my heart.

69Remembrance of Your feet removes all sorrows.
What sorrow have I, Prabhu, — You are in my house!"

70The Lord was pleased with Duhkhini's words
and began to speak to her with sweet words.

71The Lord says: "Listen, mother, go into the house:
I am hungry — cook quickly."

72Then Sri Duhkhini Devi, hearing the Lord's words,
herself went into the house to cook.

73Thakura Pandita brought many kinds of provisions,
and the devi joyfully began to cook.

74Rice, vegetable dishes and various sweets,
pishtakas and the like she cooked, and paramanna too.6

75Cleaning the place, she set out two seats
and, arranging two meals, placed [them] there.

76Then Jagadisha, with great joy in his heart,
made his request before the two Lords:

77"Prabhu, Duhkhini has finished cooking;
be merciful, come and eat, both of You."

78Hearing this, Mahaprabhu and Prabhu Nityananda
joyfully go to eat.

79Seeing two meals, the Lord Gaurahari says:
"Bring and arrange one more meal."

80Hearing this, a seat was placed in that spot,
and one more meal was arranged, brought and set there.

81Seeing this, Mahaprabhu rejoiced in His mind
and speaks some sweet words to Jagadisha:

82"I have heard all the people saying to one another
that a certain craftsman came to your house

83and fashioned an image of Me;
you worship Him, regarding Him as Me.

84Duhkhini tends and cherishes Him,
and He calls Duhkhini mother."

85Hearing this, Jagadisha and Sri Duhkhini
make no reply: both fell silent.

86Seeing them both abashed, the Lord Gaura Raya,
the Lord, began to speak without any pretence:

87"You have both done well; have no worry at all.
I pervade everything; I am present everywhere.7

88In wood, in stone or in clay —
in whatever a devotee worships Me with devotion,

89in that, by the power of the devotee's devotion, I abide;
I fulfil the desires of devotees — in this there is nothing else.

90Whoever says that there is a difference
between Me, My devotee and My Deity

91surely goes to hell.
Without guile I have told you the essence of the truth.8

92Therefore, giving up all worry,
worship My Deity, regarding Him as Me.

93Bring My Deity — I shall see [Him]:
we three shall eat in one place."

94Hearing this, Jagadisha became exceedingly happy;
he brought the Lord's image and seated [Him] there.

95The two Lords at the sides, Nityananda in the middle:
he looks at the faces of the two Lords, filled with bliss.

96Nityananda Raya, ever intoxicated with prema for Gaura,
now looks towards the Lord Gauranga,

97now again gazes at [His] image;
seeing no difference at all, his mind is full of supreme bliss.

98Seeing the two Mahaprabhus together,
he, well pleased, says to Jagadisha:9

99"Blessed, blessed are you, Jagadisha, I tell you:
two Gauras have appeared in your house!

100Who has the power to understand your greatness?
Only he understands it who has firm devotion to Gaura's feet."

101Having said this, Sri Nityananda Himself
took hold of Jagadisha and embraced [him] in prema.

102Having embraced [him], He speaks in sweet words:
"Only now has your good fortune become known.

103Which [of Them] is the original form Himself, which the manifested one?
The two are one; there is no difference at all, that is certain."

104Hearing this, Sri Gaura-Gopala speaks these words:
"Leave other talk aside, Prabhu, and eat."

105Then the two Mahaprabhus and Nityananda —
all three ate joyfully.

106Having rinsed Their mouths, the three sat on the seats;
Jagadisha brought fragrant paste and flowers and applied [them] to [Their] bodies.

107Then he laid the three to rest in three places
and in turn served [Their] feet.

108Then the three great Lords fell asleep,
and Jagadisha went and honoured the mahaprasada.

109Then he himself sat down to nama-sankirtana,
while Duhkhini remained in meditation on Gauranga's feet.

110Then Gaura-Gopala woke from sleep;
calling for His mother, He cries and plays all sorts of pranks.

111Hearing this, Duhkhini Devi went there
and, taking Gopala on her lap, gave Him the breast.

112At this time Nityananda woke from sleep
and saw Gaura-Gopala on Duhkhini's lap.

113Nityananda began to speak to Duhkhini:
"Mother, you have made your human birth fruitful.

114The mother of the Lord Gauranga is Shachi Thakurani:
until now we knew only this.

115Now I have seen: Gaura is your son.10
Your good fortune, mother, cannot be put into words.

116Blessed, blessed is Mahaprabhu Sri Krishna Chaitanya!
Who else will understand this hidden lila of Yours?

117Blessed, blessed is Jagadisha, blessed is Sri Duhkhini!
The earth will be filled with your fame."

118In this way [He] praised Duhkhini.
At that time the moon set, and the night passed.

119Mahaprabhu rose and called out "Hari!" —
and Gaura at once got up from Duhkhini's lap.

120Then the three Lords rose and performed Their morning duties,
and Mahaprabhu asked Duhkhini for leave to go.

121Mahaprabhu says: "Mother, be glad at heart
and give Me leave: I shall go to Nilachala.

122I am one Gaura, and this is Gaura-Gopala:
in two forms I am present in your house at the same time.

123Whichever form you wish, keep that one here;
the other form will go on pilgrimage to the holy places.

124Let Gopala go, and I shall stay in your house,
or I shall go, and you keep Gopala."11

125These words Mahaprabhu spoke to Duhkhini.
Hearing them, the devi took Gopala onto her lap.

126Seeing [this], Mahaprabhu says: "Listen, Duhkhini:
now I set out on pilgrimage to the holy places."

127Having said this, Mahaprabhu and Prabhu Nityananda,
having consoled Duhkhini, joyfully depart.

128Glory, glory to Mahaprabhu Sri Krishna Chaitanya!
Glory to the merciful Prabhu Nityananda — He is blessed!

129For the fulfilment of the devotees' desire is the manifestation of the Two;
They fulfilled the longing of Duhkhini Devi.

130Blessed is my Prabhu Jagadisha, the jewel of virtues!
Blessed is Duhkhini Thakurani, the purifier of the world!

131Gaurachandra descended in the city of Navadvipa —
[and it is they] in whose house He abides again in the form of a prakasha.

132Jagadisha and Duhkhini are the Lord's associates;
at the feet of those two I bow again and again.

133Having described all these lilas, being an insignificant soul,
[I pray:] Prabhu, out of compassion forgive [my] offences.

134I am utterly destitute, my mind ever wicked;
I am poor, low and fallen, and moreover devoid of bhajana.12

135I have no power to describe, my mind is not pure:
it is Bhagavatananda's mercy that makes [me] describe.

136That Prabhu mercifully makes me write:
by my own power this description would not come about.

137Bhagavatananda is the master of my master;
may I serve his two feet birth after birth.13

138Hoping in his mind to obtain the dust of his feet,
Ananda has described the manifestation of Gaura-Gopala.

Thus in the Charitra-vijaya of Sri Jagadisha Pandita ends the tenth varna, called "The Account of the Manifestation of the Deity Sri Gaura-Gopala in the Village of Sri Yashoda".

Notes

  1. The edition reads «এবে নীলাচলে আসি করিব গমন» (ebe nīlācale āsi kariba gamana); «আসি» (āsi, "having come") is apparently a misprint for «আমি» (āmi, "I"). Cf. 121.
  2. Shantipura is the place where Advaita Acharya lived. On the Lord's stay after sannyasa in Advaita's house at Shantipura see CC Madhya 3; see also varna 9, note 3.
  3. «প্রতি মূর্ত্তি» (prati-mūrti, 13, 18 and below) — "image", "likeness": a Deity in which, by the Lord's word (14), He Himself dwells. From 62 on this Deity is called Sri Gaura-Gopala. The author tells of His manifestation as a miracle (20–34): a craftsman sent by the Lord manifests the Deity in a single night and departs.
  4. «জাতিতে ভাস্কর» (jātite bhāskara) — "a craftsman by caste (jati)". The craftsman's name is not given.
  5. Cf. varna 7 (Duhkhini nurses the little Nimai in Navadvipa) and varna 6, note 9: the author apparently identifies Jagadisha Pandita of Yashoda with the Jagadisha of the pair "Jagadisha and Hiranya", the Lord's neighbours in Navadvipa in His childhood.
  6. Pishtaka (পিষ্টক, piṣṭaka) — cakes made of rice flour. Paramanna — rice cooked in milk with sugar (see varna 9, note 7).
  7. The edition reads «সর্বত্র ব্যবকর আমি» (sarvatra byabakara āmi); the reading is unclear. Taken as «ব্যাপক» (byāpaka), "all-pervading".
  8. Cf. the well-known verse cited as words of the Padma Purana: arcye viṣṇau śilā-dhīr guruṣu nara-matir vaiṣṇave jāti-buddhiḥ… yasya vā nārakī saḥ — "One who regards the Deity of Vishnu as stone, the guru as an ordinary man, a Vaishnava as belonging to a caste… is a dweller in hell."
  9. «দুই মহাপ্রভু» (dui mahāprabhu, 98, 105) — the Lord and His Deity Sri Gaura-Gopala; in 108 «তিন মহাপ্রভু» (tina mahāprabhu, "the three great Lords") — together with Nityananda.
  10. Nityananda's words praise Duhkhini's vatsalya-prema (Gaura-Gopala at her breast). Shachi-devi remains the mother of Mahaprabhu; these words do not diminish her position.
  11. In the edition the punctuation in 124–126 is shifted («…তব ঘরে।» / «…গোপালেরে।» / «…কহিলা ॥» / «…লইলা।» / «…দুঃখিনী ॥» / «…আমি।»); the couplets are arranged by rhyme (ঘরে/গোপালেরে, কহিলা/লইলা, দুঃখিনী/আমি).
  12. «সদামন্দ মন» (sadāmanda mana) is taken as «সদা মন্দ মন», "a mind ever wicked"; «হীনাধাম» (hīnādhāma) as «হীন অধম», "low, fallen".
  13. The line of disciples: Jagadisha → Raghunatha Acharya → Bhagavatananda → Premananda → Radhacharana → Ananda Dasa; the author's guru is Radhacharana. "The master of my master" is as in the text. The author's signature (138) is a variant of the formula.
